I'l' toss in my few cents here. It will be programmed to take the least destructive path. What parameters or datum the car bases this call on is not known, but you get the idea. NO SYSTEM IS PERFECT! The idea that self driving cars will prevent death altogether and not minimize it is crazy thinking. I have worked in software development and I can tell you that even something "secure" and "stable" for years is not without error ontop of any threat of hacking or tampering. Using multiple systems to keep decision in check is optimal, yes. But no system is perfect and there is no guarantee death will not occur.

I am against automation, but in this case minimizing deaths is a matter of safety that I think supplants automation in terms of importance. A sophisticated automatic car that minimizes death is the best we can hope for. There may be an instance when a car makes a decision and kills someone as a result, but the converse is that if there were 10 similar instances and only 1 of them ended in harm as opposed to 10 instances and n>1 people dying due to human error, the car is more valid on the street than a human in terms of safety.

TL;DR automated cars should minimize death, but can never remove death.
